name: Wild East Brewing Co.
fitNotes: Dog-friendly indoors, has a house dog, hosts weekly food pop-ups (Fri-Sun), allows outside food. Dedicated 625 sqft event space (The Cellar) plus 2,000+ sqft taproom. Community-oriented, independently owned by three co-founders. Already collaborates regularly with pop-up vendors. Reviews highlight community feel and dog-friendliness.

name: Other Half Brewing - Domino Park
fitNotes: Major Brooklyn brewery at Domino Park waterfront. Reviews specifically mention dogs everywhere. Large indoor/outdoor space, dedicated events booking page. Higher volume and more corporate than Wild East, but huge foot traffic. Contact via form at otherhalfbrewing.com/contact.

name: Transmitter Brewing
fitNotes: Farmhouse ale brewery in the Brooklyn Navy Yard. Reviews mention a brewery dog. Outdoor beer garden, hosts parties. Smaller, more intimate feel - great for a curated event.

name: Franklin Park
fitNotes: Large beer garden and bar carved from a former mechanic shop. Massive outdoor space, two bars in connected buildings. Long history of hosting events (trivia, reading series, DJ nights). Reviews mention dogs at outdoor tables. Actively solicits private party requests. Contact via form at franklinparkbk.com/contact.

name: TALEA Beer Co. (Cobble Hill)
fitNotes: Female-founded brewery with gorgeous, spacious taproom and mezzanine event space. Dogs allowed in outdoor seating only (not indoors). Dedicated events program. More polished and brand-forward. Has hosted events up to 110 people. Contact via form at taleabeer.com/pages/contact-us.

name: Gold Star Beer Counter
fitNotes: Beloved neighborhood beer bar in 11238. Reviews describe the crowd as 'new parents, dog owners, remote workers'. Sidewalk seating, vinyl records, craft sandwiches. Small but perfect for an intimate pop-up with the exact right demographic. Contact via form at goldstarbeercounter.com/contact.

name: Beastie Bestie Pet Provisions
fitNotes: Independent pet store with cat adoption lounge in back. Community-focused, supports local rescue. Good foot traffic on Franklin Ave. Pet portrait event directly serves their customer base. Contact via website form.

name: MR. FRIENDLY - Bed-Stuy Pet Supply
fitNotes: 100% BIPOC-owned holistic pet supply store with strong brand identity and aesthetic. Makes accessories by hand on-site. Has 'Curb Creamery' for pet ice cream. Very intentional about community and brand collaborations. Perfect audience overlap and brand alignment.

name: Pet Club
fitNotes: Clean, well-curated independent pet store with three locations. Staff is knowledgeable and community-oriented. DM on Instagram is their primary contact method. Multiple locations means potential for repeat collaborations.

name: From Here to Sunday
fitNotes: AAPI woman-owned gift shop and gallery featuring 125+ local artists. Extensive pop-up history - the business was literally built through pop-ups before going brick-and-mortar. Already carries prints, zines, and paper goods from local makers. Near-perfect fit for screen printed pet postcards. Centers marginalized voices and collaborates with local artists and causes.

name: Greenlight Bookstore
fitNotes: Beloved independent bookstore that regularly hosts events, author readings, and community programming including an annual Where's Waldo neighborhood hunt partnering with 40+ local businesses. Carries gifts and paper goods alongside books. Very high foot traffic on Fulton. Founded 2009.

name: Established Gallery
fitNotes: Contemporary art gallery with monthly shows and group exhibitions. Community-oriented and accessible atmosphere. Could host a pet portrait event or exhibition. Need to confirm Instagram and email.

name: Aura Coffee and Bar
fitNotes: Tagged as a 'dog cafe' on Google. Listed as event venue. Community-oriented with plant-filled space. Small but high vibe. Good weekend hours. Need to confirm Instagram and email.

name: Hungry Ghost
address: 781 Fulton St, Fort Greene, Brooklyn, NY 11217
fitNotes: Established local coffee chain with devoted neighborhood following. Strong foot traffic on Fulton. Good sidewalk visibility for a pop-up table setup. More of a 'set up outside' opportunity than a hosted event.

name: Habana Outpost
fitNotes: Iconic Fort Greene outdoor gathering spot and community institution. Massive outdoor space, well-established history of events and gatherings. Seasonal but extremely high foot traffic when open. Need to confirm Instagram and email.
